findings.label: validation
findings.failure_mode: An unclosed bash fence in Brief probes whose visible content is syntactically valid bash causes BRIEF_BLOCK (no heading reset, unlike sibling awks) to accumulate past the missing close to EOF, absorbing the Dependencies prose harmlessly; bash -n then reports no syntax error and validate-pack.sh exits 0 despite the fence never being closed.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:63 — BRIEF_BLOCK awk has no /^## /{f=0} reset, only f&&b&&/^```/{exit} to stop
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:26 — sibling WIRING_FENCES awk resets f=0 on the next heading for comparison
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:65 — bash -n runs over whatever BRIEF_BLOCK captured, with no separate 'fence closed' check for Brief probes
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:60-68 — an unclosed fence containing only valid-syntax bash followed by ordinary Dependencies prose never triggers fail()

findings.label: validation
findings.failure_mode: An earlier unclosed fence anywhere in the file desyncs the file-wide fence toggle used by the citation check, causing later real sections (Label probes, Dependencies) to be treated as inside a fence and dropped from citation scanning; a bare unwrapped citation in that swallowed region is never checked or flagged.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:74 — STRIPPED=$(awk '/^```/{f=!f;next} !f' "$PACK") toggles per raw fence marker with no heading anchor
tests/packs/bad-wiring-unfenced.md:11 — opening fence in Wiring files never closed before the next ## heading
tests/packs/bad-wiring-unfenced.md:14-21 — Label probes heading/table falls inside the mis-toggled 'in fence' state and is excluded from STRIPPED
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:76-79 — BARE_CITES is derived only from STRIPPED, so a bare citation in the excluded region is never scanned

findings.label: validation
findings.failure_mode: Prose outside a fenced block containing a URL such as 'https://github.com/user/repo.md' is matched by the bare-citation regex once matching resumes past the disallowed ':' in the scheme, producing a slash-containing non-backtick match that trips fail(), rejecting a pack over a legitimate URL that was never a bare file citation.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:76 — bare-citation regex has no scheme/protocol exclusion
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:77 — grep -v '^`' | grep '/' keeps any non-backtick match containing a slash, including a URL fragment
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:81 — fail("citation not backtick-wrapped...") fires on the matched URL fragment

findings.label: duplication
findings.failure_mode: The new Brief-probes validation hand-copies the exact same awk extraction script that build-artifacts.sh already uses (build-artifacts.sh:351) to pull the same bash block out of the same section, instead of sourcing one shared implementation. If the section's heading text, fence convention, or block-closing rule ever needs to change, a fix applied to one copy can miss the other, so a pack that build-artifacts.sh parses one way can be validated a different way by validate-pack.sh — the exact drift shape this codebase later fixed by factoring the equivalent heading-check logic into a single sourced file (model/pack-heading-check.sh).
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/build-artifacts.sh:351 — already extracts the Brief probes bash block for eval
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:63 — hand-copies the identical awk script into a second, independent file
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:64-67 — the copy is used only to run bash -n on the block, with no shared source between the two extractions

model/pack-heading-check.sh:1-10 (later state of this same repo) — records this exact pattern, two independently hand-typed copies drifting apart, as the accepted duplication defect this file was created to stop recurring
